display.purpose: Study title, section headings, and large readings.

body.purpose: Navigation, labels, instructions, and interface text.

reading.purpose: Timestamps, camera IDs, and measured values.

motion.name: latest-sample-ring
motion.purpose: Quietly marks fresh endpoints while following a live confidence stream; paused, offscreen, hidden, historical, stale, and reduced-motion states remain still.

motion.name: capture-replay
motion.purpose: Advances only through actual camera captures and stops at gaps over ten seconds; reduced motion switches immediately.

motion.name: scene-angle
motion.purpose: Moves the schematic to a second view angle; reduced motion switches immediately.

components.name: Crossing replay instrument
components.description: Axonometric crossing model, fixed schematic pedestrian state, selected camera capture, detector confidence rails, reported dwell ruler, and real-sample replay controls.
components.css: .instrument { color: #faf9f5; background: #1d304f; border-radius: 6px; overflow: hidden; } .road-top { fill: url(#road-top); } .marking { fill: #e6e3d9; } .scene-person { opacity: 0; transition: opacity .2s ease-out; } [data-presence=pedestrian] .scene-person { opacity: 1; } .scene-readout { border-left: 1px solid #586983; } .measure-track i { transition: width .22s ease-out; }

components.name: Confidence timeline
components.description: Time-based comparison of device and YOLO confidence with a selected sample and timestamp-aligned warning markers.
components.html: <svg id="chart" role="img" aria-label="Confidence by capture time"><path class="series series-device" d="M0 80 L100 45 L200 55"/><path class="series series-yolo" d="M0 90 L100 60 L200 65"/><path class="event" d="M200 12 208 20 200 28 192 20Z"/></svg>
components.css: #chart .series { fill: none; stroke-width: 2; stroke-linecap: round; stroke-linejoin: round; } #chart .series-device { stroke: #182844; } #chart .series-yolo { stroke: #615a91; stroke-dasharray: 5 4; } #chart .point-device { fill: #182844; } #chart .point-yolo { fill: #fff; stroke: #615a91; stroke-width: 1.5; } #chart .event { fill: #f9ebe7; stroke: #ab4438; stroke-width: 1.7; }

components.name: Camera selector row
components.description: Selected source is identified by a filled radio-like marker and a restrained violet-tinted row.
components.css: .camera { padding: 13px clamp(18px, 2vw, 32px); border-top: 1px solid #cbd0db; } .camera.is-selected { background: #f1f2f8; } .camera-head button[aria-pressed=true]::before { background: #615a91; box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 2px #fff; border-color: #615a91; }

components.name: Action buttons
components.description: Thin ruled dashboard controls and a deep blue save action; admin controls keep a 44px touch height.
components.html: <button class="button" type="button">Pause</button><button class="button admin__primary" type="submit">Save changed settings</button>
components.css: .button { min-height: 38px; padding: 8px 12px; border: 1px solid #cbd0db; border-radius: 4px; background: #fff; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 600; } .admin .button { min-height: 44px; padding: 8px 13px; font-size: 13px; } .admin__primary { background: #1d304f; color: #fff; border-color: #1d304f; }

components.name: Settings field
components.description: Persistent label, monospace value, and range hint; edited and invalid states remain distinct.
components.css: .field input, .field select { min-height: 44px; padding: 8px 10px; border: 1px solid #536078; border-radius: 4px; color: #182844; background: #fff; font: 14px/1.45 ui-monospace, monospace; } .field[data-dirty=true] :is(input,select) { border-color: #615a91; background: #f0f0f7; } .field[data-invalid=true] :is(input,select) { border: 2px dashed #ab4438; background: #f9ebe7; }

components.name: Admin feedback
components.description: Text-first live feedback with restrained violet or coral full-border states.
components.css: .admin__toast:not(:empty) { padding: 10px 16px; border: 1px solid #cbd0db; border-radius: 4px; background: #fff; } .admin__toast[data-tone=good] { border-color: #615a91; } .admin__toast[data-tone=bad] { color: #ab4438; border: 1px solid #ab4438; background: #f9ebe7; }

components.name: Live sample marker
components.description: An expanding ring marks the newest fresh point while the user follows the live camera stream.
components.css: #chart .point-live-ring { fill: none; stroke: #615a91; stroke-width: 1.2; transform-box: fill-box; transform-origin: center; } .plot.has-live-sample.motion-active .point-live-ring { animation: latest-sample-ring 1.8s cubic-bezier(.16, 1, .3, 1) infinite; } @keyframes latest-sample-ring { 0% { transform: scale(.72); opacity: .82; } 100% { transform: scale(2.15); opacity: 0; } }

components.description: A pale pedestrian crosses silver-lilac lane marks on the study's deep blue plate.

narrative.overview: An annotated field instrument for studying pedestrian camera captures. An axonometric crossing model, actual camera capture replay, and linked presence, confidence, and dwell readings lead the view; the confidence timeline and recorded warnings remain inspectable.
keyCharacteristics: Axonometric crossing cutaway with explicitly schematic camera view and pedestrian position
Replay of actual selected camera frames, stopped at long gaps without invented interpolation
Device and YOLO confidence on the same percentage scale, with reported dwell against its configured limit
Elapsed-time plot with distinct solid and dashed detector traces, labeled axes, and a live endpoint ring
Timestamp-aligned coral warning diamonds with written status and event-specific snapshots
Warm paper surfaces, fine rules, condensed headings, and monospace measurements
rules: The Trace Distinction Rule: device and YOLO confidence remain distinguishable by line style and point fill as well as color.
The Recorded Event Rule: warning markers and images use the warning record's own timestamp and snapshot.
The Live Marker Rule: animate only fresh newest samples while following the stream; stop when paused, hidden, offscreen, historical, stale, or reduced motion is preferred.
The Replay Truth Rule: change the pedestrian symbol, image, and readings only from the selected stored capture; never imply a measured path or calibrated position.
dos: Keep scene geometry visibly schematic and label the fixed pedestrian as untracked.
Keep replay synchronized with the chart, capture timestamp, image, and selected camera.
Stop replay at long gaps rather than implying motion between missing frames.
Use the violet endpoint ring only for fresh data while Latest is active.
Keep graph time horizontal and confidence vertical from 0 to 1.
Pair warning color and shape with a written label.
donts: Do not invent camera names, footage, or measurements.
Do not use a single color as the only distinction between the two detector traces.
Do not imply that the model's camera frustum or pedestrian anchor is measured geometry.
Do not invent a walking path or intermediate frames.
